recentItems.title: El Salvador's Bukele Hacks Haiti Gangs To Death, Inside Nayib's Total War To Bleed Crime Bosses Dry
recentItems.description:
The kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians in Haiti has triggered something that few could have anticipated: an aggressive military intervention by a Central American country thousands of kilometres away. What began as a search-and-rescue mission has rapidly evolved into a full-scale offensive against some of Haiti's most powerful criminal gangs.On October 18, 2026, four Salvadoran personnel disappeared after their armoured vehicle came under attack near Port-au-Prince. But El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele was not prepared to let the incident pass quietly. He responded by sending additional troops, threatening Haiti's gang leaders with overwhelming force and eventually backing helicopter-led attacks against gang strongholds. Then came November 10. Helicopters struck properties associated with the notorious 400 Mawozo gang, marking a dramatic escalation in the campaign. And suddenly, Bukele, a controversial leader known for his uncompromising war on gangs at home, began receiving praise from Haiti's own leadership. But is this the beginning of a breakthrough in Haiti's seemingly endless security crisis? Is Bukele emerging as the leader capable of doing what international missions have struggled to achieve? Or is this intervention opening a dangerous new chapter in Haiti? Well come along and watch this edition of From The News Desk with Yash Goyal to know the entire picture.
